[THOUGHT]  
The patient presents with a 4-month history of chronic, non-bloody, mucoid diarrhea and lower abdominal cramping that improves with defecation — classic functional bowel symptom patterns. Crucially, there is *no weight loss, fever, nocturnal diarrhea, anemia (Hb 13 g/dL normal), fatigue, extraintestinal manifestations, or objective signs of systemic illness*. The mild leukocytosis (WBC 11,000/mm³) with neutrophil predominance is nonspecific and can occur in acute or subacute infection — but notably, *all objective inflammatory and serologic markers are pending/unreported*: fecal calprotectin, CRP, tTG-IgA, and Giardia antigen test. - Diarrhea intermittently associated with mucus

- No weight loss  
- No nocturnal diarrhea  
- No fever

- No prior GI diagnoses or surgeries  
- No current medications or drug allergies  
- Absence of reported abdominal tenderness, swelling, or perianal lesions  
- Normal hemoglobin (13 g/dL), arguing against chronic blood loss or malabsorption-related anemia  
- Mild leukocytosis (WBC 11,000/mm³) is nonspecific and not diagnostic of infection or inflammation in isolation  

[GAPS]  
- Fecal calprotectin result — needed to objectively exclude intestinal inflammation (e.g., IBD, microscopic colitis)  
- Stool Giardia antigen test result — required to confirm or rule out chronic giardiasis  
- Serum tTG-IgA — needed to exclude celiac disease, a key mimic of chronic diarrhea  
- CRP — adjunctive marker of systemic inflammation  
- Stool culture, ova & parasite exam, or PCR — to broaden infectious workup beyond Giardia  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Irritable Bowel Syndrome with diarrhea predominance (IBS-D)
